How we work

What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 01

    1–2 weeks

    Discover

    We sit with credit operations, collections, service, claims, advisory or risk teams to map how customers actually apply, pay, claim and complain, and which systems hold the data. We confirm what the LOS, LMS, insurer portals, RTA feeds and gateways allow through APIs or exports, review the current consent and channel setup, and choose the first journey.

    Deliverables

    • Current journey map with handoffs, delays and drop-offs
    • System and integration inventory with access options
    • Regulatory touchpoints for the chosen journey, for the compliance officer to confirm
    • Prioritized automation shortlist with indicative effort
    • Baseline measures for the chosen journey

    What we need from you

    • Read access or exports from the LOS, LMS, broker system, MF back office or gateway
    • Time with operations, credit, collections, claims or risk leads
    • Current templates, call scripts, policies and grievance process
    • WhatsApp Business account, DLT registrations and 1600-series number status
  2. 02

    1–2 weeks

    Design

    We design flows, customer pages, checklists, routing rules, response targets and approval points, and write WhatsApp, DLT SMS and email templates. Consent wording, KYC handling, data localization, retention and the exact point where each person decides are designed with the client's compliance officer before anything is built.

    Deliverables

    • Flow diagrams with human decision points marked
    • Template drafts for WhatsApp, DLT SMS and email
    • Data map covering consent, minimization, localization, retention and access
    • AI scope, refusal rules and the approved document set
    • Acceptance criteria and test scenarios

    What we need from you

    • Consent and privacy notice wording reviewed by the client's legal or compliance owner
    • Approved product documents, policy wordings, KFS formats and scripts
    • Decisions on owners, escalation paths, contact windows and response targets
  3. 03

    2–6 weeks

    Build

    We build workflows in n8n or code, secure customer pages and staff consoles, retrieval-based assistants over approved documents, and the connections to client systems. Everything runs in a staging setup with masked data, hosted in India wherever the data or the regulator requires it.

    Deliverables

    • Working workflows and integrations in staging
    • Secure customer pages and staff consoles
    • AI prompts with evaluation sets and refusal rules
    • Monitoring, alerts, audit logs and error handling

    What we need from you

    • API credentials or sandbox access for core systems
    • Masked sample data for testing
    • Feedback from team leads on console usability
  4. 04

    1–2 weeks

    Validate & launch

    Teams test real scenarios: a blurred PAN card, a bounced mandate, a motor claim reported at night, a stale risk profile, a chargeback close to its deadline. We evaluate AI answers against approved documents, confirm contact windows and consent checks, launch on one product, branch or team first, and train every shift.

    Deliverables

    • Test results against acceptance criteria
    • AI evaluation report on groundedness and handoffs
    • Training and quick reference guides
    • Go-live checklist and rollback plan

    What we need from you

    • Staff time for scenario testing and training
    • Sign-off from the business owner and the compliance officer
    • Templates approved by Meta and registered on DLT
  5. 05

    Ongoing, reviewed monthly

    Operate & improve

    We monitor workflow health, deadlines, contact-rule checks and AI quality, fix failures, and review results with the client each month. Regulatory changes, such as revisions to RBI's recovery rules or TRAI's TCCCPR, are reviewed with the compliance officer and reflected in rules and templates.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly performance and exception review
    • Workflow health and failure alerts
    • Template, prompt and rule change log
    • Roadmap for the next journey or product

    What we need from you

    • A named business owner for decisions
    • Notice of changes to products, policies, systems or regulations
    • Feedback from frontline teams and customers

Suggested first pilot

One product, one journey, four to six weeks

We start where volume and pain are highest. For a lender that is usually checklists, secure uploads and status updates for one product, before the full KYC tracker. For a broker it is motor and health renewals, for an advisory firm onboarding and risk profiling, and for a fintech onboarding drop-off recovery or a dispute queue for one dispute source. A baseline taken in the first week makes the comparison honest.

  • One product or team and one customer journey
  • Approved WhatsApp and DLT SMS templates and a secure customer page
  • Integration with the LOS, broker system, MF back office or gateway in read and limited write mode
  • A staff console for the queue, with escalation to a named owner
  • Weekly check-ins and a go or no-go review at the end of the pilot

Governance

Safe by design, owned by your team.

  • Consent is recorded per purpose and channel, service and marketing consent are kept separate, and a withdrawal on any channel applies across WhatsApp, SMS, email and calls.
  • PAN, Aadhaar, account and card numbers never enter chat, Slack alerts or AI prompts. Documents go through secure pages with role-based access and India-hosted storage, and card data stays with the gateway, which narrows the PCI DSS scope the business carries.
  • AI drafts, classifies, summarizes and routes on model deployments the compliance team approves. Credit, underwriting, claims, suitability, collections settlements and fraud decisions are made and recorded by named, qualified people.
  • Contact rules are enforced in the workflow: permitted calling hours, customer preferences, 1600 and 140 number series, DLT templates and opt-outs, with every exception logged and reviewed.
  • Templates, prompts, content and rule changes are versioned and approved by the compliance officer before going live, and records are kept for the applicable regulatory retention period.
  • Failures and missed deadlines raise alerts, AI answers are sampled monthly against approved documents, and access is reviewed each quarter and whenever staff leave.

Compliance notes

The obligations that shape the design.

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025

Identity, financial and health data in loan, insurance and investment journeys is personal data. Automations are designed around clear notice, purpose-bound consent, minimal collection, security safeguards, breach response and deletion when the purpose ends, alongside the longer retention financial-sector laws require. The Rules were notified on 13 November 2025 in phases, with most obligations applying eighteen months later, around May 2027. Not legal advice.

meity.gov.in · Source ↗

RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025

The lender assesses creditworthiness itself, gives a KFS before the contract and sends digitally signed loan documents, offers a board-set cooling-off exit of at least three days, or one day for loans under seven days, and lends and collects through bank accounts directly. Data collection must be need-based with explicit consent, apps may not access contacts, files or call logs, data stays in India, and recovery agent details reach the borrower before contact.

rbi.org.in · Source ↗

RBI fair practices and recovery conduct

RBI's 2025 Responsible Business Conduct Directions require communication in a language the borrower understands, written loan terms, a recovery grievance route, and agents who carry a notice, authorization letter and identity card. Recovery calls before 8 am or after 7 pm, persistent calls and harassing relatives count as harassment, and microfinance loans have narrower hours. RBI has since amended its recovery rules, so we check the version in force.

rbidocs.rbi.org.in · Source ↗

IRDAI policyholder protection, advertisement and claims rules

IRDAI's 2024 policyholder protection regulations and master circulars require advertisements, including those issued by intermediaries, to be fair and not misleading under board-approved advertisement policies, plus a Customer Information Sheet, a free-look period and defined service and claim timelines. For health claims, insurers must decide cashless requests within one hour and final discharge authorization within three hours. Claim decisions stay with insurers.

irdai.gov.in · Source ↗

SEBI rules for investment advisers, AI use and finfluencers

SEBI-registered advisers must assess and share each client's risk profile before advising, keep advice suitable and preserve records for at least five years. Since the December 2024 amendments, advisers must tell clients how far AI tools are used in their advice, and SEBI-regulated entities remain solely responsible for AI outputs and client data. Regulated entities may not associate with unregistered advisers or with anyone making unpermitted return or performance claims.

sebi.gov.in · Source ↗

Calling numbers, DLT and WhatsApp rules for financial messaging

TRAI directions from late 2025 require banks, NBFCs, insurers, mutual funds and other regulated financial entities, in phases by sector, to make service and transactional calls from 1600-series numbers. Promotional calls use 140-series numbers, SMS uses DLT-registered headers and templates, and TRAI amends these rules often. WhatsApp requires opt-in and approved templates outside the 24-hour window, and its policies prohibit debt collection and restrict some loan products.

trai.gov.in · Source ↗

Questions

Frequently asked.

Will the system approve or reject loans, policies or claims?

No. It collects, checks and routes information and keeps customers informed. Credit officers, underwriters, insurers, advisers and fraud analysts make every decision and record the reason. Where a prospect sees indicative eligibility, it is based on your published criteria and clearly labeled as not a decision. RBI's Digital Lending Directions also require the lender to assess creditworthiness itself and bar credit limit increases without the borrower's explicit consent.

Can we send EMI reminders and collection messages on WhatsApp?

Pre-due reminders and payment confirmations can go as approved utility templates to borrowers who opted in. WhatsApp's Business Messaging Policy lists debt collection among prohibited uses, so overdue follow-up runs on DLT SMS, email, app notifications and calls from 1600-series numbers by trained staff within permitted hours. WhatsApp also restricts some loan products, such as payday-style loans, so each use case is checked against the current policy before launch.

Do we need to replace our LOS, broker system or MF back office?

No. We connect to the systems you already use through their APIs, integration partners or scheduled exports. Where a system allows only limited access, we design around it, for example by preparing data for staff to confirm rather than writing into the system directly. Naming a system on this page does not imply a partnership with its vendor.

How do you handle KYC documents, Aadhaar and card data?

Documents are uploaded on your own domain or fetched through DigiLocker or CKYC by your regulated entity, stored encrypted in India, visible only to permitted roles, and kept for the period your KYC and record-keeping obligations require. We never ask for Aadhaar, PAN, account or card numbers in chat, Aadhaar numbers are masked in line with your KYC policy, and card payments stay with your gateway or payment aggregator, outside our tools.

Can an AI assistant answer policyholder, borrower or investor questions?

Yes, within limits. It answers only from documents you approve, such as policy wordings, Customer Information Sheets, charges schedules and FAQs, shows where each answer comes from, and hands over to a person for account-specific requests, complaints, claims, grievances and any question about what to buy or sell. SEBI-registered advisers must tell clients how far AI tools are used in their advice and remain responsible for the output, so the assistant is configured to stay out of advice.

Do you help advisers and agents with marketing content?

Yes, through a reviewed content workflow: drafts written only from approved source material, required disclosures added, phrases such as assured returns flagged, and your compliance officer's approval before anything is published or shared. We do not arrange finfluencer tie-ups or promotions that make return or performance claims, which SEBI's rules on association with unregistered persons prohibit for regulated entities.

How long until something is live, and what does it cost?

Most first pilots run four to six weeks from kickoff to a live journey for one product or team. Cost depends on the systems involved, the integrations your vendors allow and the journeys in scope, so we quote after the Discover phase rather than publishing a fixed price.

We also serve customers outside India. Does this work with GDPR or similar rules?

The same principles apply: purpose-based consent, minimal data, clear retention and access controls, and human review of significant decisions. If you serve people in the EU or UK, GDPR may apply alongside India's DPDP Act, and RBI requires payment system data to be stored in India, so we configure hosting, notices, consent records and deletion rules in a way your legal adviser can confirm against each regime.
